info.title: How SIP Trunks Work
info.body: A SIP trunk connects {appName} to your telecom provider (e.g. STC, Mobily, Zain in Saudi Arabia, or global providers like Telnyx and Bandwidth). Once configured, assign it to a phone number on the Phone Numbers page, then your AI agents will place and receive calls through the trunk, no Twilio required.
info.requirements: Requirements: Asterisk must be installed on your server. After adding or modifying trunks, click "Reload Asterisk" to apply the configuration.

dialog.manualHint: Configure host, port, and credentials without using a preset.
dialog.transportHint: Check your provider's docs. Most use UDP.
dialog.usernameInvalid: The SIP username can't contain {chars}. Use only letters, numbers, and . _ - + (if your provider gave you an email address as the username, ask them for a plain username instead).
dialog.dialPrefixHint: Optional tech prefix added before the number when dialling
dialog.stripPlusLabel: Send numbers without the + sign (some PBXs reject a leading +)

debug.title: SIP Debug
debug.description: Diagnose SIP problems without SSH access — health checks run on the server, and call events stream below.
debug.endpointNotLoaded: Endpoint not loaded — calls will fail with "Allocation failed". Click "Reload Asterisk".
debug.providerUnreachable: Provider unreachable — calls will fail with "Allocation failed". Usually a wrong transport/port for this provider (e.g. Twilio needs UDP 5060 or TLS 5061, not TCP).
debug.providerNotQualified: Provider not qualified yet (no OPTIONS ping result)
debug.noContact: No contact registered for this trunk in Asterisk. Click "Reload Asterisk".
debug.healthFailed: Could not load health checks. Is the backend running?
debug.noEvents: No SIP events yet. Make a test call or reload Asterisk — events will appear here.

toast.savedNotLoaded: SIP trunk saved, but Asterisk did not load it

checks.ownHost: That's the address of this server's own Asterisk: the one you give your carrier so it can send calls to you. Enter your carrier's SIP host here instead. Calls through this trunk would be sent back to this server and fail.
checks.hostPlaceholder: SIP Host still has the preset's placeholder text. Replace it with the host your provider gave you.
checks.hostFormat: Enter only the host name or IP address in SIP Host (for example sip.telnyx.com). Leave out sip:, usernames and paths, and put the port in Port.
checks.realmPlaceholder: Auth Realm still has placeholder text. Replace it, or leave it blank.
checks.portRange: Port must be a number from 1 to 65535 (usually 5060).
checks.tlsOn5060: TLS normally uses port 5061; port 5060 is for UDP and TCP. Check your provider's settings.
checks.port5061NotTls: Port 5061 is normally for TLS. With UDP or TCP, use 5060 unless your provider says otherwise.
checks.ipHostDomainRealm: SIP Host is an IP address but Auth Realm is {realm}. For most carriers the SIP Host is that same domain. Make sure the IP is your carrier's and not the address you were given for inbound calls.
checks.usernameNoPassword: There's a username but no password. Most carriers refuse calls without both (error 401 or 407).
checks.passwordNoUsername: The password is ignored without a username.
checks.stripPlusWithPrefix: With a Dial Prefix set, numbers are always sent without the +, so the "without the + sign" option changes nothing.
